messages:
maya: Hey team — I'm drafting a new Grafana dashboard to compare rack PDU power draw with GPU utilization. Need 3 things: a per-rack watts timeseries, a per-rack GPU util overlay (right axis), and an alert for high-power + low-util. PR with initial layout: https://git.internal/redwood/dashboards/pull/482 :eyes:
liam: Ack. Which Prometheus metrics do we actually have for PDU and GPU util?
chris: We export pdu_sensor_watts{pdu,host,rack} from our pdu collectors and nvml_gpu_utilization{gpu,host} from nvml-exporter. Host -> rack label exists on node metrics.
sophia: For the overlay, easiest is two queries and use dual axes in Grafana. Left axis = W, right axis = % util. We can use a template var $rack.
maya: I tried to mash something but hit a vector mismatch: 
```promql
sum by (rack) (avg_over_time(pdu_sensor_watts[5m])) / on(host) group_left(rack) avg_over_time(nvml_gpu_utilization[5m])
```
Doesn't work — dividing by host vectors.
liam: Right — don't divide different dimensional vectors. Better: compute two separate series grouped by rack and render them together. Example: Q1 = `sum by (rack) (avg_over_time(pdu_sensor_watts[5m]))` and Q2 = `avg by (rack) (avg_over_time(nvml_gpu_utilization[5m]))`.
chris: Also useful to show moving averages to smooth noise: 
```promql
avg_over_time(sum by (rack) (pdu_sensor_watts)[30m])
```
(or wrap with increase/irate if you want power deltas).
maya: Good call. For the alert rule I sketched: trigger when PDU > 3000W and avg GPU util < 20% for 10m. Can someone sanity check PromQL?
liam: Here's a clean alert expression you can use: 
```promql
(sum by (rack) (avg_over_time(pdu_sensor_watts[10m])) > 3000)
 and on(rack) (avg by (rack) (avg_over_time(nvml_gpu_utilization[10m])) < 20)
```
Label it with severity=warning, runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/power-lowutil.
sophia: For the dashboard: - add template var $rack (multi) - left axis unit=W, right axis unit=% - add horizontal threshold lines (power warning at 3000W, temp critical at 85C)
maya: Also want a small heatmap panel for thermal spike density per rack (1m buckets) using nvml_gpu_temp_celsius. Anyone want to propose a PromQL for spikes?
chris: You can do something like: `increase((nvml_gpu_temp_celsius > 80)[5m])` but Prometheus doesn't support boolean in increase. Better: `sum by (rack) (count_over_time((nvml_gpu_temp_celsius > 80)[10m]))` — that'll show number of samples above 80C per rack.
jonathan: I'll take the PR for panel placement and JSON layout. Plan to put PDU watts (stacked if multiple PDUs), GPU util overlay, temp heatmap, and a small table of per-tenant power attribution (from label tenant_id on workloads exporter).
sophia: UI nit: use distinct colors for PDUs, and use dashed line for 80% util threshold. Also add units and short tooltips describing derivation (e.g., "PDU = sum of sensors per rack").
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Dashboard branch dashboards/rack-power-util-1718501234 deployed to staging for review.
liam: I'll run the alert through the flapping detector in staging — set for 10m window with 2m for suppression while we tune. Will also add a holdback so it doesn't page on transient test runs.
maya: Thanks all. Once staging looks good, can we promote to prod during the next maintenance window? I'll add to infra sync agenda. @liam please validate that alert noise is low over 48h.
liam: Yep — will monitor and report back.
chris: Added runbook link to the alert rule and a short remediation checklist: check PDU breakers, verify tenant jobs, fallback to secondary PDUs.
maya: Perfect. Closing notes: PR updated with the suggested PromQL and panel variables. Linking here: https://git.internal/redwood/dashboards/pull/482 — feel free to comment on panel sizing. :thumbsup:
